fix.summary:
Current construction is not complete/correct. Both Review-020 Spec findings are sustained, with these bounded dispositions:

1. Require the concrete code-review recipe—not the generic V1 schema—to grant every constructed leg `bash` plus that accepted dispatch’s byte-exact canonical `range.diffCommand` (`git diff <resolved-base>...<pinned-target>`). Validate this after canonical range derivation and before acceptance/runner effects; omission from either the task-bound ceiling or a leg request must reject the whole proposal as a correctable capability preflight failure. Keep the schema law that arrays may be empty and that `bash` may have zero commands; those shapes remain representable but are insufficient for this recipe. Update `README.md` to remove the claim that bash/the diff command are optional for an accepted review leg, and replace the current acceptance assertions in `test/reviewer-dispatch.test.ts` with red cases for no-bash, empty-bash, and one-leg omission plus a green case where both legs carry only the necessary exact command. Do not require unrelated shell commands or widen grants.

This reconciles the earlier receipts substantively: review-011’s “unrequested restriction” and review-012’s contradictory headings are not authority. The canonical Skill requires both child prompts to carry the full diff command, while the compiled prompts carry no diff bytes and the fixed child-tool vocabulary offers no other diff reader. A no-bash/zero-command leg therefore cannot perform the review it is dispatched to perform. U3’s least-privilege law requires the necessary operation and forbids extras; it does not authorize an underpowered grant. This is also the executable-policy form of C2. Generic schema optionality does not override recipe validity.

2. Remove live object-database disambiguation for abbreviated hexadecimal bases in `src/reviewer-pinned-git.ts`. Resolve a prefix uniquely only among commit identities derived from immutable activation roots—at minimum the commits reachable from captured `targetHead`, since accepted bases must be its ancestors—then retain the existing commit and ancestry checks. Unrelated objects added after reader activation must neither create ambiguity nor alter the result. Preserve current full-SHA, captured symbolic-ref, and captured HEAD-relative behavior. Add a concrete regression in `test/reviewer-pinned-reader.test.ts`: activate the reader, record successful abbreviated-base resolution, add an unreachable colliding object without changing HEAD or captured refs, and prove the same prefix still resolves identically; also prove multiple matching reachable commits reject. Do not add a second pin/drift mechanism or a test-only production hook.

`npm run typecheck` and the 54 focused Reviewer tests pass on head `381ca14`, but the passing suite explicitly accepts the first defect and has no post-activation collision counterexample, so it does not discharge either finding.

details.note: The later docket-only commits do not change the reviewed production seams. Finding 1 is a recipe minimum, not a widening of the capability schema; finding 2 violates the accepted immutable-pin chronology directly.
